title: Hailee Steinfeld Casts a Spell: Disney's 'Hexed' and a Record-Breaking Year
summary:
Hailee Steinfeld is having a moment — and she's not keeping it a secret. The actor and singer stopped by The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon to promote Hexed, Walt Disney Animation Studios' upcoming film where she voices the lead character, Billie Doe.

"It's such a dream come true," Steinfeld said. "You jump at the opportunity to be a part of a Disney animated original." She revealed she started the project while pregnant and finished it after welcoming her baby girl, Harper Haize, in April. "It was really such an amazing, transformative time in my life."

Billie, she explained, is a "rebellious, unconventional teen" who discovers she's a witch with magical powers. Steinfeld described Hexed as a "magical, magical coming of age story and a story of self-discovery and learning to use that magic within you — and that power within you — for good." The film arrives this Thanksgiving.

That's not all. Steinfeld starred in Ryan Coogler's 2025 vampire flick Sinners and contributed the track "Dangerous." The film earned 16 Academy Award nominations — an all-time record — and won four. She missed the ceremony but watched from home with a "bowl of popcorn and big belly." She also talked about the movie's relentless night shoots and sang the praises of director Coogler.

As for rumors she'll return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe in Avengers: Doomsday? Steinfeld stayed coy. "Time will tell," she said. She previously appeared in Hawkeye and voiced Spider-Gwen in the Spider-Verse films.

Steinfeld's big break came in the Coen Brothers' True Grit, which earned her an Oscar nomination for best supporting actress. As a recording artist, she's landed five entries on the Billboard Hot 100 since her debut single "Love Myself" reached No. 30 in 2015, and her Haiz EP charted on the Billboard 200 that same year.

She also played the "Don't Say the Same Thing Challenge" with Fallon — a game where they name things in a category without saying the same answer.
why_it_matters: Steinfeld's schedule — a Disney animated lead, a hit horror film, charting singles and a rumored superhero return — shows how the modern entertainment industry runs on performers who work across studios and platforms at once, and how casting a star can turn an unreleased movie into an event before anyone has seen it.

background_read: Walt Disney Animation Studios (the division behind Frozen, Encanto and Zootopia, separate from Pixar, the studio behind Toy Story) has spent decades building animated films around celebrity voices. Because animation takes years, actors typically record their lines long before a movie reaches theaters, which is why Steinfeld could start work on Hexed while pregnant and finish after her daughter was born.

The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon (a long-running NBC late-night talk show) is a standard stop on a press tour: actors appear months before a film opens to promote first looks and trailers, often playing a comedy game like the one Steinfeld took part in.

Hailee Steinfeld first became widely known as a teenager in the Coen Brothers' Western True Grit, earning an Academy Award nomination for best supporting actress. The Oscars are voted on by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and remain the industry's most-watched awards ceremony.

Billboard (an American music-industry magazine) publishes the Hot 100 singles chart and the Billboard 200 albums chart, both based on sales and streaming — so saying an artist 'charted' is a measurable industry claim, not just an opinion.

Ryan Coogler (the director of Fruitvale Station, Creed and Black Panther) is known for working repeatedly with the same performers and for filming physically demanding scenes, which fits Steinfeld's description of the 'relentless night shoots' on his vampire movie.

perspectives.description: Disney gains a recognizable, musically trained star for an original animated film, and audiences get a performer who can carry both songs and story. Steinfeld benefits too: a Disney lead, a charting single and award-season buzz reinforce each other and widen what she can be cast in next.

Celebrity voice casting can crowd out trained voice actors who build entire careers in animation, and press tours like this are essentially marketing dressed as conversation. Focusing on the star can also bury the hundreds of animators, writers and sound artists who actually make the film.

Disney has cast famous faces in animated films for decades — from Robin Williams in Aladdin to pop stars in more recent musicals — because a known voice sells tickets. Steinfeld's career fits a newer pattern: performers who move between franchises, indie films, animation and the music charts rather than staying in one lane.

The next questions are whether Hexed launches a franchise, whether Steinfeld really returns to the Marvel Cinematic Universe, and how quickly changing animation and AI tools reshape what voice work looks like. If studios rely even more on celebrity names, the industry's labor and pay debates will likely sharpen.
